paragraphs.text: A loose [Anhua dark tea](anhua-dark:definition) from 2022, made from wild-harvested leaf rather than garden-grown. Anhua is a mountain county on the Zi river in north-central Hunan, a protected place of origin and widely named the main home of dark tea in China.

Like every tea from the county, it starts as [heimaocha](anhua-dark:making), the raw dark tea: large leaf fixed, rolled, piled, rolled again and dried. From there it keeps changing. Dark tea is [post-fermented](dark:definition): after the leaf is made, warmth, moisture, microbes and the leaf's own chemistry keep working on it.
At four years, this one is early in that change. The trade keeps Anhua tea for years because it is said to improve, but no agreed count of years makes it [aged](anhua-dark:ageing).

brewing.text: In a small pot or gaiwan, use water at the boil and start with a steep of about 15 to 30 seconds, a little longer each round. Pressed and aged Anhua tea is also commonly simmered in a pot.

notice.text: Pine smoke or pine resin above all, a sweet taste and aftertaste, and a mellow, thick, smooth cup; a liquor from yellow and orange to orange-red. Young tea is often smokier in the first infusions and a little bitter, sweetening as the infusions go on.
